decision.case_state: Ticket NBL-021 (mp_time). Landlord Quinn approved the lock replacement and four new keys on 2024-11-21 (event 006). Provider Alder Compliance was assigned (event 010, 2024-11-21). No visit date is booked. On 2024-11-22 the provider asked for the resident's contact details to book the visit (event 015). Outstanding: tenant's direct number and availability; provider visit booking; lock replacement and four keys (two tenant, one office, one landlord).

next_actions.action: Reply to Alder Compliance with the contact on file exactly as written (07700 900625, enter this code when calling) and say we are confirming the tenant's best number and times and that the work is approved.
Ask the tenant Clara Jenkins for her best contact number and available times for the lock replacement visit, and say Alder Compliance will contact her.
Return the job to auto mode after handling the provider message.
Review on 2024-11-25 whether the provider has booked a visit and the tenant has replied; chase the provider if no date is set.

boundaries: Sending the contact on file does not confirm a visit date or any completed work.
The tenant's direct number has not been verified.
No cost or quote exists, so the cost of the lock and keys is not yet known.
Key handover to the office and the landlord has not happened and is not established.
remaining_work: Tenant to reply with best number and times (agency owns the chase).
Alder Compliance to contact tenant, book the visit and report the result; quote if the work needs one.
Keys: confirm the two office/landlord keys reach the office.
Invoice and final checks, then close with tenant confirmation and landlord informed.
missing_info: Tenant's direct phone number and availability.
Lock/key cost (no quote yet; the approval gave no cap).
Attachment-85-document referenced at event 012 is unavailable and was not seen.
decision.summary: The landlord approved the key and lock replacement with four keys on 2024-11-21 and Alder Compliance was assigned. On 2024-11-22 the provider asked for the tenant's contact details to book the visit; I sent the contact on file with its calling code to the provider, asked the tenant for her best number and times, returned the job to auto, and set a review for 2024-11-25.

answers.question: Where does this case stand right now, and what is outstanding?
answers.answer: Approved and assigned to Alder Compliance, but no visit is booked. The provider needs the tenant's contact and availability. Outstanding: the visit, the lock replacement, the four keys (two tenant, one office, one landlord), the invoice and final checks.

answers.question: What is the next action, who is it for, and through which channel?
answers.answer: Email to Alder Compliance with the contact on file (A1); email to tenant Clara Jenkins asking for her best number and times (A2); resume auto (A3); review on 2024-11-25 (A4).

answers.question: Does anything need a human decision, and why?
answers.answer: No. The landlord's approval covers the work with no spend cap, and the steps are routine. Escalation is only needed if the cost later exceeds what the landlord agreed or the visit fails.

actions_claimed.description: Sent Alder Compliance the contact on file with the calling code, and confirmed the approved work.
Sent tenant Clara Jenkins a message asking for her best contact number and times, and saying Alder Compliance will contact her.
Scheduled a review on 2024-11-25 to check the visit booking and the tenant reply.

conflicts: The job description says the contact should be the tenant's, but the provider's contact line gives a number with a calling code; I passed it on exactly as written and did not treat it as verified.
assumptions: The 07700 900625 number on file is the tenant's contact, as the job email carries it.
The landlord's approval 'approves the maintenance action... and requests new keys' covers the lock replacement and four keys, with no spend cap.
